case.cs1.title: Fuel prices in Guatemala
case.cs1.desc: From a price-sign photograph to a refuelling recommendation, with every value traceable back to the image it came from.
case.cs1.subtitle: Extraction, forecasting and recommendation, traceable end to end.
case.cs1.problem.title: The problem
case.cs1.problem.body: When to fill the tank. Not what it costs today, which the sign already says, but whether waiting a week works out better or worse. The answer is forecast 1, 2 and 4 weeks ahead from photographs of petrol station price signs.
case.cs1.turn.title: What changed the approach
case.cs1.turn.body: The assumption was that reading the prices would be mechanical. Looking at the crops, 10 of 16 contained no display, and on the ones that did, the reader returned 4??8 where the sign said 43.19. The cause looked like perspective; rectifying changed nothing. The digits are italic by typographic design. Correcting the slant took digit accuracy from 0 to 4 out of 5. But the deeper lesson was different: extraction is never going to be complete, and that is not a defect to fix but the shape of the problem.
case.cs1.lineage.title: A value you cannot trace is worthless
case.cs1.lineage.body: Every price declares where it came from: read from a photo, recovered from a receipt total, interpolated between two real readings, imputed, or generated. That provenance travels all the way to the model as an input, because an imputed value and a read one are not worth the same. And the chain back to the original image is foreign keys, not a field someone maintains, so it cannot drift. Faced with a bad recommendation, you can tell whether the model failed or the reading did.
case.cs1.delivery.title: What ships
case.cs1.delivery.body: An installable package and a container image, published from the same tag and carrying the same version number. Whoever installs it can run the full flow from an empty folder, without cloning the repository.
case.cs1.stack.title: Decisions the rest rests on
case.cs1.stack.a: Deterministic seven-segment reading, no GPU. A heavy vision model was tried and dropped: 1.5 GB of weights and a repository that swapped the weights under the same branch, so downloading it twice gave different models under the same name.
case.cs1.stack.b: No image enters version control. The data lives outside and is fetched; the repository holds code and documentation.
case.cs1.stack.c: The quality gate fails the run, it does not report. A model that cannot beat the naive baseline does not pass.
case.cs1.stack.d: Publishing requires manual approval. A released version cannot be replaced, only withdrawn, and what is irreversible is what you stop to look at.
case.cs1.open.title: What is still open
case.cs1.open.body: The extraction figures come from 16 photographs and will not carry a conclusion. With the full history, the share of valid readings has to be measured again, and that measurement decides whether a trained detector is needed instead of more rule tuning. The threshold is fixed in advance at 70%, so it cannot be moved after seeing the result.
workshop.a01.title: scikit-learn pipeline
workshop.a01.desc: Extraction, filtering, type handling and train/test splitting, with dimensionality reduction. Packaged as an installable library, with its notebook.
workshop.a03.title: Hyperparameter tuning
workshop.a03.desc: Linear regression with grid search, evaluation against standard metrics, and analysis of overfitting and coefficients. Packaged as an installable library.
page.workshops.empty: Both workshops live in the repository, with their code and notebooks.
case.cs2.title: Club BI points system
case.cs2.desc: Diagnosing a bank's rewards system with nobody left who designed it: reconstructing the data architecture from the outside and proposing where to optimise it.
case.cs2.subtitle: Diagnosis, data architecture and a miniature replica of a bank loyalty programme.
case.cs2.problem.title: The brief
case.cs2.problem.body: Optimise the Club Bi points system run by Banco Industrial, under one condition: the people who designed it no longer work at the company. Before optimising anything, the team had to establish what the system does, and the only evidence available was what the bank publishes. Every documented rule carries its confidence level: public, inferred or assumed.
case.cs2.turn.title: What changed the approach
case.cs2.turn.body: The earning rate turned out to be public, but it is not written down in any single place. It lives in a footnote repeated on each product page: 1 point per US$1, and 1 per US$10 at supermarkets, petrol stations and three other categories. Of eight ways to earn points, only one publishes its rate. The missing rulebook stopped being an obstacle to the research and became the first finding.
case.cs2.arch.title: Three architecture decisions
case.cs2.arch.a: The balance is a set of lots, not a counter. Points expire in a yearly cut-off on 5 February and the miles conversion depends on the product that earned them, so every point needs its month and its origin.
case.cs2.arch.b: The grain is the family group. Family pooling makes the balance belong to the group, and only the account holder can redeem it.
case.cs2.arch.c: Eligibility does not travel with the transaction. Membership, mobile banking, card enrolment and campaign sign-up are looked up at crediting time, and without a history of those states the past cannot be recomputed.
case.cs2.replica.title: The miniature replica
case.cs2.replica.body: A notebook rebuilds the pipeline on synthetic data: four sources, Bronze, Silver and Gold layers, an engine that reads its rules from the catalogue, and a lot ledger with redemption and expiry. The findings are measured on that replica: the advertised two-year validity runs from 13 to 25 months, the same spending yields three different balances depending on where the annual cap applies, and prize-draw points are the only ones that cannot be rebuilt from another source.
case.cs2.findings.title: Main findings
case.cs2.findings.a: Points are not interchangeable. The miles conversion depends on the product that earned them, yet all six balance channels show a single number.
case.cs2.findings.b: The reduced rate lands on everyday spending. Supermarkets and petrol stations earn a tenth as much, and the rule is disclosed in an asterisk.
case.cs2.findings.c: The rate is set in dollars while purchases settle in quetzales, at an exchange rate the bank does not publish.
case.cs2.findings.d: The points portal accepts four-character passwords and returns a balance from nothing more than an ID number.
case.cs2.ml.title: Where a model fits
case.cs2.ml.body: The first addition is an LLM that classifies the merchant category when its code is missing, with output restricted to a closed catalogue. It is the only one that fixes a calculation: a wrong category costs a factor of ten in points. The replica already measures its baseline metric, points credited at the wrong rate. Anomaly detection and redemption propensity come later, because they observe a system that has to be right first.
case.cs2.open.title: What is still open
case.cs2.open.body: Thirteen questions only the bank can answer, among them the exchange rate used for earning, the rate for average balances, and whether the annual cap applies per card, per customer or per group. The assumptions standing in for them live in a separate file, so each answer is absorbed by changing one value and re-running the notebook.
